newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: U.S. agrees to Manila phone rate cut request.
newsitem.headline: U.S. agrees to Manila phone rate cut request.

text.p: The United States has acceded to the request of Philippine telecommunication companies to defer reduction of rates charged on overseas calls, a top U.S. official said on Monday.
The rate currently stands at $1 per minute of overseas calls and the money paid by callers is shared among call providers.

"We are talking about how the changes will be accomplished, how the transition can be structured and over what period of time it ought to take place," US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) chairman Reed Hundt told reporters after talks on the issue with local telephone lephone companies.
Local companies have been lobbying for deferment of the rate cut, saying they need the money to finance their expansion programmes.
The US FCC earlier called for an immediate reduction of the rate in order to be competitive with newer technology which does not use the network of the telecommunication firms.
